title: From a tally of next words to a neighbour in vector space
brief: Smooth a bigram table, match it with a softmax, scatter-add an embedding gradient, and train a window model and a skip-gram on a tiny notebook.
hints: bigram_counts: np.add.at into a (V, V) array of zeros. An assignment leaves a repeated pair at 1.
add_k_probs: add k to every cell, then divide by the row sum with keepdims=True. Adding k only on positive cells leaves an unseen word at probability 0.
mean_nll is the mean of -np.log(probs[prev, nxt]). perplexity is np.exp of that mean, so a uniform 1/V model returns the vocabulary size.
row_softmax subtracts the row max before exp. embedding_backward must np.add.at, because a repeated index has to accumulate.
skip-gram loss is softplus(-dot) plus softplus(dot) on each noise vector. The center gradient is (sigmoid(dot) - 1) times the real context, plus sigmoid(dot) times each noise vector.

Draw tables with default_rng(seed).normal(0, 0.1). The window model divides the logit gradient by the number of windows. The skip-gram draws the center table before the context table and rejects a noise index equal to the real context.
